# Comparaison t-test vs Wilcoxon avec tableau dans Power BI
# ============================

library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

# ---- Préparer les données 2025 ----
data_2025 <- dataset %>%
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date)) %>%
  filter(year(Date) == 2025)

if(nrow(data_2025) < 3){
  stop("Pas assez de données pour effectuer les tests.")
}

# ---- Test de normalité Shapiro-Wilk ----
shapiro_result <- shapiro.test(data_2025$value)

# ---- Test t unilatéral supérieur ----
t_test_result <- t.test(data_2025$value,
                        mu = 0.2,
                        alternative = "greater")

# ---- Test de Wilcoxon unilatéral supérieur ----
wilcox_result <- wilcox.test(data_2025$value,
                             mu = 0.2,
                             alternative = "greater")

# ---- Préparer un tableau récapitulatif ----
test_table <- data.frame(
  Test = c("Approche paramétrique", "Approche non-paramétrique"),
  P_value = c(signif(t_test_result$p.value, 4),
              signif(wilcox_result$p.value, 4)),
  Commentaire = c(
    ifelse(shapiro_result$p.value >= 0.05, "Paramétrique recommandé", "Normalité douteuse"),
    ifelse(shapiro_result$p.value < 0.05, "Non-paramétrique recommandé", "Paramétrique possible")
  )
)

table_grob <- tableGrob(test_table, rows = NULL, theme = gridExtra::ttheme_default(
  core = list(fg_params = list(cex = 0.9)),
  colhead = list(fg_params = list(cex = 1, fontface = "bold"))
))

# ---- Histogramme + densité normale ----
hist_plot <- ggplot(data_2025, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), bins = 30, fill = "skyblue", color = "white") +
  stat_function(
    fun = dnorm,
    args = list(mean = mean(data_2025$value, na.rm = TRUE),
                sd   = sd(data_2025$value, na.rm = TRUE)),
    color = "red", linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Histogramme des valeurs 2025",
    subtitle = paste0("Shapiro p = ", signif(shapiro_result$p.value, 4)),
    x = "Valeur (µSv/h)",
    y = "Densité"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# ---- QQ-plot ----
qq_plot <- ggplot(data_2025, aes(sample = value)) +
  stat_qq(color = "steelblue") +
  stat_qq_line(color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "QQ-plot",
    subtitle = paste0("Shapiro p = ", signif(shapiro_result$p.value, 4)),
    x = "Quantiles théoriques",
    y = "Quantiles observés"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# ---- Affichage combiné : histogramme + qq-plot + tableau en dessous ----
grid.arrange(
  arrangeGrob(hist_plot, qq_plot, ncol = 2),
  table_grob,
  nrow = 2,
  heights = c(3, 1) # 3/4 pour graphiques, 1/4 pour le tableau
)

# dataset = pandas.DataFrame(value, Date)
# dataset = dataset.drop_duplicates()

# Collez ou tapez votre code de script ici :
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import shapiro, ttest_1samp, wilcoxon
from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_histogram, stat_function, geom_qq, geom_qq_line, labs, theme_minimal, theme, element_text
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.gridspec import GridSpec

# ---- Filtrer les données pour 2025 ----
df = dataset.copy()  # dataset = données Power BI
df[''Date''] = pd.to_datetime(df[''Date''])
data_2025 = df[df[''Date''].dt.year == 2025].copy()

if len(data_2025) < 3:
    raise ValueError("Pas assez de données pour effectuer les tests.")

values = data_2025[''value''].values

# ---- Test de normalité Shapiro-Wilk ----
shapiro_stat, shapiro_p = shapiro(values)
print(f"Shapiro-Wilk test: statistic={shapiro_stat:.4f}, p-value={shapiro_p:.4f}")

# ---- T-test unilatéral supérieur (mu = 2) ----
t_stat, t_p_two_sided = ttest_1samp(values, popmean=2)
# Pour unilatéral supérieur
t_p = t_p_two_sided / 2 if t_stat > 0 else 1 - t_p_two_sided / 2
print(f"T-test unilatéral supérieur: t={t_stat:.4f}, p-value={t_p:.4f}")

# ---- Wilcoxon unilatéral supérieur (test sur différence avec 2) ----
# Attention : scipy wilcoxon ne prend pas directement un mu ≠ 0
diff = values - 2
wilcox_stat, wilcox_p_two_sided = wilcoxon(diff)
wilcox_p = wilcox_p_two_sided / 2 if np.median(diff) > 0 else 1 - wilcox_p_two_sided / 2
print(f"Wilcoxon unilatéral supérieur: statistic={wilcox_stat:.4f}, p-value={wilcox_p:.4f}")

# ---- Tableau récapitulatif ----
test_table = pd.DataFrame({
    "Test": ["T-Student unilatéral", "Wilcoxon unilatéral"],
    "P_value": [round(t_p, 4), round(wilcox_p, 4)],
    "Commentaire": [
        "Paramétrique recommandé" if shapiro_p >= 0.05 else "Normalité douteuse",
        "Non-paramétrique recommandé" if shapiro_p < 0.05 else "Paramétrique possible"
    ]
})
print("\nTableau récapitulatif:")
print(test_table)

# ---- Histogramme + densité normale ----
mean_val = np.mean(values)
std_val = np.std(values, ddof=1)
hist_plot = (ggplot(data_2025, aes(x=''value''))
             + geom_histogram(aes(y=''..density..''), bins=30, fill=''skyblue'', color=''white'')
             + stat_function(lambda x: (1/(std_val * np.sqrt(2*np.pi))) * np.exp(-(x-mean_val)**2/(2*std_val**2)),
                             color=''red'', size=1)
             + labs(title="Histogramme des valeurs 2025",
                    subtitle=f"Shapiro p = {shapiro_p:.4f}",
                    x="Valeur (µSv/h)",
                    y="Densité")
             + theme_minimal(base_size=12))

# ---- QQ-plot ----
qq_plot = (ggplot(data_2025, aes(sample=''value''))
           + geom_qq(color=''steelblue'')
           + geom_qq_line(color=''red'', size=1)
           + labs(title="QQ-plot",
                  subtitle=f"Shapiro p = {shapiro_p:.4f}",
                  x="Quantiles théoriques",
                  y="Quantiles observés")
           + theme_minimal(base_size=12))

# ---- Affichage combiné ----
plt.figure(figsize=(14,6))
gs = GridSpec(2,2, height_ratios=[3,1])

# Histogramme
plt.subplot(gs[0,0])
hist_plot.draw()
plt.subplot(gs[0,1])
qq_plot.draw()

# Tableau
plt.subplot(gs[1,:])
plt.axis(''off'')
plt.table(cellText=test_table.values,
          colLabels=test_table.columns,
          cellLoc=''center'',
          loc=''center'')
plt.show()

from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_line, geom_point, geom_smooth,
    scale_x_date, labs, theme_minimal, theme, element_text, xlim
)
from datetime import datetime

# ---- Données Power BI ----
df = dataset.copy()

# Conversion des dates
df[''Date''] = pd.to_datetime(df[''Date''])

# Filtrer l’année 2025
df_2025 = df[df[''Date''].dt.year == 2025]

# Agrégation quotidienne (si plusieurs mesures par jour)
daily = df_2025.groupby(''Date'', as_index=False)[''value''].mean()

# ---- Définir les bornes d''affichage ----
start_date = pd.Timestamp(''2025-01-01'')
today = pd.Timestamp(datetime.today().date())  # Date du jour

# ---- Graphique ----
p = (
    ggplot(daily, aes(x=''Date'', y=''value''))
    + geom_line(color=''steelblue'', size=0.7)
    + geom_point(color=''darkblue'', size=0.8)
    + geom_smooth(method=''loess'', color=''red'', se=False, span=0.1)
    + xlim(start_date, today)
    + scale_x_date(date_breaks=''1 month'', date_labels=''%b'')
    + labs(
        title=''Chronogramme journalier des mesures de radiation - Année 2025'',
        x=''Date (2025)'',
        y=''Valeur mesurée''
    )
    + theme_minimal(base_size=12)
    + theme(figure_size = (10, 8),
        axis_text_x=element_text(angle=45, ha=''right''),
        plot_title=element_text(weight=''bold'', size=14)
    )
)

# Affichage
print(p)
